ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the Cartesian coordinate system, $OA=OB=\sqrt{5}$, and $AB=\sqrt{10}$. If the coordinates of point $A$ are (1, 2), what are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line BN$\perp$x-axis, AM$\perp$x-axis,\\
$\because$OA=OB=$\sqrt{5}$, AB=$\sqrt{10}$,\\
$\therefore$AO$^{2}$+OB$^{2}$=AB$^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$BOA=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$BON+$\angle$AOM=$90^\circ$,\\
$\because$$\angle$BON+$\angle$NBO=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AOM=$\angle$NBO,\\
$\because$$\angle$AOM=$\angle$NBO, $\angle$BNO=$\angle$AMO, BO=OA,\\
$\therefore$$\triangle$BNO$\cong$$\triangle$OMA,\\
$\therefore$NB=OM, NO=AM,\\
$\because$the coordinates of point A are (1,2),\\
$\therefore$the coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(-2,1)}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the Cartesian coordinate system, $OA=OB=\sqrt{5}$, and $AB=\sqrt{10}$. If the coordinates of point $A$ are $(1,2)$, what are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Construct line $BN\perp x$-axis and $AM\perp x$-axis. Since $OA=OB=\sqrt{5}$ and $AB=\sqrt{10}$, we have $AO^2+OB^2=AB^2$, so $\angle BOA=90^\circ$. Therefore $\angle BON+\angle AOM=90^\circ$. Since $\angle BON+\angle NBO=90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle AOM=\angle NBO$. With $\angle BNO=\angle AMO$ and $BO=OA$, we get $\triangle BNO\cong\triangle OMA$. Hence $NB=OM$ and $NO=AM$. Because the coordinates of point $A$ are $(1,2)$, the coordinates of point $B$ are $(-2,1)$.
